lessons.text: If a V appears in a numeral, consider moving one of its diagonal sticks to turn it into an X, because this change preserves stick orientation and yields a valid Roman numeral.
lessons.label: specific

lessons.text: When moving a stick, verify that every resulting symbol is a legal Roman numeral or operator and that the stick's orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) remains unchanged.
lessons.label: specific

lessons.text: Before moving any stick, calculate the numeric values of the left‑ and right‑hand sides to see which term must be altered.
lessons.label: specific

lessons.text: Before any move, calculate the numeric values of every term and the total equation to identify which term must be altered to achieve equality.
lessons.label: specific

lessons.text: After each proposed stick relocation, verify that every resulting symbol remains a legal Roman numeral or operator and that the arithmetic equality is true; discard any move that fails either condition.
lessons.label: meta

lessons.text: Only consider one‑stick changes that turn a symbol into another legal Roman numeral or operator, preserving stick orientation (e.g., V→X by relocating a diagonal).
lessons.label: specific

lessons.text: After each candidate move, double‑check that the new equation is arithmetically correct and that all symbols remain valid; discard any change that violates either condition.
lessons.label: meta

lessons.text: If you relocate a stick, only transform a symbol into another valid Roman numeral or operator that can be made with the same orientation of sticks; e.g., a V can become an X by moving a diagonal, but not into I.
lessons.label: specific

lessons.text: If you remove a stick from a numeral, choose a component (like a solitary I) whose removal leaves another legal numeral; then place the stick where it can change an operator (e.g., turn ‘‑’ into ‘=’) while preserving its orientation (rotate if needed).
lessons.label: specific

lessons.text: List every possible one‑stick change (e.g., V→X, I→V, –→=) that leaves both the origin and target symbols valid, then select the change whose numeric effect equals the identified gap.
lessons.label: specific

lessons.text: If you need to change a Roman numeral, think of which valid symbol can be obtained by moving a single stick while respecting orientation rules.
lessons.label: specific

lessons.text: After each matchstick relocation, double‑check that the new symbols are legal Roman numerals and that the arithmetic equality holds; discard any move that violates either condition.
lessons.label: meta

lessons.text: Before moving any matchstick, calculate the integer values of all numerals and the overall equation to pinpoint which term must change.
lessons.label: specific

lessons.text: Before moving any stick, calculate the integer values of each Roman numeral and the overall equation to pinpoint which term must change to achieve equality.
lessons.label: specific

lessons.text: After applying a matchstick move, double‑check both the arithmetic result and that every symbol still conforms to the allowed matchstick shapes; reject any change that violates orientation rules.
lessons.label: meta

lessons.text: When listing one‑stick transformations, prioritize changes that keep stick orientation, e.g., converting X to V by moving a diagonal, because they produce valid Roman symbols.
lessons.label: specific

lessons.text: Before moving any matchstick, compute the numeric values of all Roman numerals and the total of each side of the equation.
lessons.label: specific

lessons.text: If you need to alter a numeral, look for a single-stick transformation that keeps the stick’s orientation (e.g., V → X by moving a diagonal).
lessons.label: specific

lessons.text: After proposing a change, double-check that every resulting symbol is a legal Roman numeral or operator and that the arithmetic equality holds.
lessons.label: meta

lessons.text: Before solving, calculate the numeric values of each Roman numeral and the overall equation to identify the exact difference that must be corrected.
lessons.label: specific

lessons.text: If a candidate move creates an invalid numeral or operator, reject it and continue testing other moves; always confirm both symbol legality and arithmetic truth before finalizing.
lessons.label: meta

lessons.text: If the equation contains a minus sign, try converting it to an equals sign by relocating a vertical stick from an adjacent I (rotating it to horizontal), which simultaneously changes the operator and reduces the numeral’s value.
lessons.label: specific

lessons.text: Systematically list every legal one‑stick transformation (including rotations) and test each one for symbol validity and arithmetic correctness before accepting a solution.
lessons.label: meta

lessons.text: If the gap can be fixed by changing an operator, move a stick from a numeral to the operator and rotate it, e.g., turn '-' into '=', ensuring both the altered numeral and operator remain valid Roman symbols.
lessons.label: specific

lessons.text: If you relocate a stick, you may rotate it; use this to change operators (e.g., turn ‘‑’ into ‘=’) or to transform numerals while preserving orientation.
lessons.label: specific

lessons.text: When a numeral contains an X, try the one‑stick change X→V (or X→I) to lower its value by 5, making sure the moved stick forms a valid V and the remaining symbol stays legal.
lessons.label: specific
